content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" leasing plan in the United States at the end of this month. The report points out that this move marks "one of the largest changes in the way Apple sells devices in history."

Here's how it works.

Lower monthly payments to purchase hardware

Apple is partnering with Klarna to support the new Apple Upgrade plan. Consumers will need to undergo a soft credit check.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will operate "like a subscription service" and apply to purchases of iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch. However, the plan comes with certain restrictions. The report notes that Apple Watch SE, the basic iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo will not be eligible for Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, the lease term for iPhone and Apple Watch is 24 months, while the lease term for Mac is 36 months.

Mark Gurman explains:

Unlike the iPhone Upgrade Program, Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare coverage. Bloomberg further points out that Apple plans to stop accepting new applications for the iPhone Upgrade Program at the same time it launches Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will officially launch on July 28, one week from now.

Apple raised the prices of iPad and Mac last month, and the new iPhone expected in September is also anticipated to see a price hike. Apple Upgrade will provide customers with an option to cope with price increases, allowing them to choose as needed.
